Iteration 0022 produced four partial sessions, used 2,642,518 input tokens and merged no task output ([record](history/records/0022.json)).
The useful checkpoint is #195 at `fbcdb75`: its report records 33 materialized controls and passing structural checks ([report](history/sessions/195/87551b569115f0f13d295518dae8e3856fd1dc2ee2edeca74d8a28c2e29541f4.md)).
Later sessions restarted from stale `task/189`, repeating work despite that checkpoint.
Inspection found #195 predates landed lineage; integration conflicts in the two preparation JSON files and includes tracked bytecode.
[Orders](orders.json) now resume #195 through its retained tag, preserve main’s lineage and split evidence, combine preparation pins and remove bytecode.
Expected gain: challenge preparation available for independent review, with the evaluator listing only baseline missing.
Verification checks deterministic generation and preparation references without LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT; failures must be reported without redesigning fixtures.
[Policy memory](../policy/working-memory.md) records the checkpoint, recovery instructions and actual model usage; routing remains unchanged without measured quota evidence.
Startup diagnostics were within budget: 12,612 estimated tokens, status ok.
Native fidelity, computation, typedef-impact, diagram differences and substantive split/baseline evidence remain incomplete; product quality is unmeasured.
Synthetic fixture generation and green structural checks establish neither benchmark readiness nor successful challenge execution.

## What next
After landing, inspect the accepted commit and Verification, then order independent substantive challenge review, preferably from a different model family.
If interrupted, resume the newest saved checkpoint; avoid restarting from task/189 or repeating whole inventories. Reader work and scorer work remain gated.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
